title: AI alert triage in the SOC
summary: Security teams drown in alerts. An agent gathers evidence for each one so analysts only see what matters.

steps.label: alert
steps.title: An alert fires
steps.text: The SIEM collects logs from every system and raises alerts. Large companies get thousands a day; most are harmless.
payload: Encoded commands are a common way to hide intent.

steps.label: lookup IOCs
steps.title: Enrich: is this known-bad?
steps.text: The agent decodes the command, pulls out indicators (domains, IPs, hashes) and checks them against threat-intelligence feeds.

steps.label: host context
steps.title: Enrich: what else happened on the machine?
steps.text: Read-only queries to the endpoint tool: parent process, network connections, other alerts on this host.
payload: Word launching PowerShell usually means a malicious document.

steps.label: verdict + evidence
steps.title: A ready-made case for a human
steps.text: Instead of a raw alert, the analyst gets a verdict, the reasoning and the evidence, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
payload: isolate host · reset user password · block domain

steps.label: isolate host
steps.title: The human pulls the trigger
steps.text: Containment can disrupt the business, so a person approves it. False positives get auto-closed with the agent's notes, saving hours a day.
